metadata.notes: Added 2026-08-16, closing a real, previously-missing step: crispy-french-fries.json and salted-fried-potatoes.json both went straight from FRY to SALT with nothing removing the clinging surface oil in between — real technique always drains fried food before seasoning (salt doesn't adhere well to an oily surface, and excess oil is unappetizing left on). REMOVE's own removalMethod parameter (data/actions/remove.json) already names 'poured_out'/'strainer_drain' as real draining techniques, but REMOVE only fires against an instance currently tracked inside a PLACE (recipe-runner.ts's placeContents) — most recipes in this vocabulary, including both forcing cases here, don't use the FILL/PLACE_IN/HEAT_PLACE machinery at all, so a PLACE-dependent verb would be unreachable for them. DRAIN is deliberately standalone, like REST — works on any isDrainable instance regardless of whether a place is involved.
metadata.methodNote: Two genuinely different techniques with a REAL, cited outcome difference, not just presentation preference: 'wire_rack' (elevated over a tray, air circulates on all sides, oil drips away) preserves crispness — draining on flat 'paper_towel' instead traps steam against the food's underside (limited surface area for oil to actually leave, and once the towel saturates the food sits in a shallow pool of its own drained oil), producing a real, commonly-observed soggy-bottom result the wire-rack method avoids. See REFERENCES.md — multiple convergent consumer food-science sources corroborate the STEAM-TRAPPING mechanism; a specific 'X% oil reduction' figure was found during research but not used here, being an isolated, unsourced number from a low-confidence source, not corroborated elsewhere. 'colander_shake' is the bulk, coarser equivalent (a whole batch shaken in a colander/strainer at once) rather than individual-piece technique — informational only, same non-enforcement depth as every other categorical parameter in this vocabulary.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): a bounded, discrete act (lift and shake, or set down on a rack/towel) — the same class as PEEL/CUT, not an open-ended do-until process like REST. Real elapsed draining time varies (seconds to a couple of minutes) but the ACT itself is a one-off, not a continuously-monitored threshold.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true — engine.ts guards addsTag against duplicates, so re-running this after an interruption is a silent no-op, not a double effect, the same reasoning INFUSE/REST already document for their own addsTag outputs.

verification.description: No pooling or visible sheen of oil remains on the surface or underneath the piece

hazards.note: The food is already out of the oil by this point (a real hazard REMOVE/PLACE_IN already declare), but hot oil still clings to and drips from a just-fried piece while transferring it to a rack or towel — a real, lower-severity residual version of the same hazard, not a new one.
